title: Unexpected fallback path selected for multi-tenant routing leading to customer errors
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Summary: Between 2026-03-09 22:18 UTC and 2026-03-10 02:40 UTC, several paying customers observed 502/504 errors and large latency spikes caused by a routing fallback path that routed requests to a quantized model variant incompatible with the customer's request schema and region. Symptoms included increased client-side timeouts, sudden token-price anomalies in billing dashboards, and downstream application errors in customers' systems.

Observed behavior: The router selected an available pool that matched availability but ignored the compatibility filter for structured-output-capable variants. For customers pinned to hosted regions with strict model capabilities, this resulted in requests being sent to a model variant lacking function-calling/structured output and running in a different region with higher network latency. The routing decision surfaced as a fallback because the primary Dedicated pool had transient capacity markers set by an autoscaler race.

Impact: High — three enterprise customers experienced production failures (support tickets #CS-2187, #CS-2193, #CS-2201). One customer reported failed checkout flows for 12 minutes. Financial and SLA risk due to incorrect tier/region routing.

Root cause: A multi-factor race between policy evaluation cache invalidation and autoscaler capacity updates caused the router's evaluation to read a partially-applied policy blob. Specifically: (1) capacity update wrote a ‘saturated’ marker to service-discovery, (2) policy-merge task started and partially replaced capability filters, (3) the route-evaluator read the new capacity marker but the old capability filter due to non-atomic reload. The non-atomic swap allowed the fallback comparator to prefer a lower-tier quantized variant in a different region because capacity was flagged but capability-match returned stale.

Reproduction steps: 1) Seed a tenant with pinned-model capability requirement (structured_output=true) and dedicated pool pinned to eu-west-1. 2) Simulate autoscaler transient spike and force a capacity marker flip on the dedicated pool. 3) Apply a policy merge that updates capability filters but delays a full reload (introduce artificial latency in policy-merge). 4) Send requests and observe route evaluation logs (router.trace) selecting a quantized-hosted variant in us-east-1.

Temporary mitigation deployed: At 2026-03-10 01:05 UTC we rolled forward a guard: route-evaluator now rejects candidate pools if capability-match is older than capacity-timestamp by more than 5s. That immediately prevented further misroutes while we work the permanent fix.

Desired permanent fix: Ensure atomic policy swap or attach versioned capability/timestamp pairs to policy blobs so evaluation is linearizable. Also add end-to-end tests simulating interleaved capacity and policy changes.

Notes: Affected code paths: route-evaluator (go/services/router), policy-merge worker (python/infra/policy), service-discovery writer (go/services/discovery).
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Shah: Triage notes — customer escalations received via Support at 22:30 UTC. Initial rollback attempted but blocked by incompatible policy state. Opening ENG ticket and paging oncall.

2026-03-10 01:10 UTC Jorge Alvarez: Deployed temporary guard to route-evaluator (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/1423) which checks capability/timestamp ordering; smoke-tested against QA tenant, observed correct routing for pinned model cases.

2026-03-10 03:00 UTC Alex Mercer: Confirmed customer-facing errors cleared after guard. Logged impacted customers in CS tickets. Action: collect traces and end-to-end logs for a one-week window for postmortem.

2026-03-11 09:20 UTC Jorge Alvarez: Root cause analysis completed — race condition between policy-merge and service-discovery writes. Draft PR for atomic policy swap ready: https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy/pull/998. Needs design review from infra team.

2026-03-12 14:00 UTC Melissa Cho (SRE): Observability updates — added a new router.trace metric annotated with policy-version and policy-timestamp. Grafana panel updated: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abcd-routing/route-eval-overview

2026-03-13 10:40 UTC Priya Shah: Eng/PM sync — proposed timeline: merge atomic-swap PR, run canary in staging, deploy to hosted, then schedule dedicated/private rollouts staggered over a week. Also propose adding explicit customer-facing SLA note for routed fallbacks in docs.

2026-03-13 15:00 UTC Jorge Alvarez: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy/pull/998 updated with infra feedback. Integration tests added to simulate concurrent capacity + policy updates (tests/policy/race_test.go).
remediation: Short-term: guard in route-evaluator rejecting stale capability matches (deployed 2026-03-10 01:05 UTC). Long-term: implement atomic swap for policy blobs (PR #998) and pair policy blobs with monotonic version/timestamp metadata. Add integration tests that simulate interleaved capacity/policy updates and include in CI gating. Plan staged rollout: staging canary -> hosted baseline -> dedicated non-critical tenants -> dedicated high-SLA -> private (customer-specific) with coordinated customer notifications.
postmortem_next_steps: Merge PR #998 and validate in staging canary (owner: Jorge Alvarez, ETA: 2026-03-16)
Add integration test suite for concurrent policy/capacity updates and enable in CI (owner: Eng-Infra, ETA: 2026-03-18)
Create runbook entry for route-evaluator stale-policy detection and mitigation (owner: SRE, ETA: 2026-03-20)
Notify affected customers with a brief post-incident summary and SLA remediation offers (owner: Customer Success, ETA: 2026-03-14)
Add dashboard alert for metric: router.policy_mismatch_rate > 0.5% sustained (owner: Observability, ETA: 2026-03-17)
notes: This ticket differs from previous misroute incidents — the distinguishing factor is a non-atomic policy reload combined with immediate capacity flips, not a stale cache TTL. We should update policy-merge infra to prefer atomic replaces or write-ahead manifests to avoid partial reads. Consider expanding chaos tests to include policy-write delays.
